- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: next forecast = prior forecast + 0.5×(true - forecast).  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overcorrection.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently below true outcome by >3% over 5+ days, shift forecast upward by 1–2% per day to catch momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (±0.3 or more) and forecast is flat, adjust for momentum: add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is rising, subtract if falling.
